sources.title: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
sources.access_utc: UNKNOWN exact request timestamp; independent reviser access occurred within the bounded window in independent_review_access.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official RFC, then inspected the manifest/completeness definitions, custom-tag rules, hash support/default modality, and filename normalization and Windows/Unix interoperability sections. Read only; no BagIt tool or validator was run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A payload manifest lists each payload path and digest. Completeness and checksum validity are separate. BagIt 1.0 creation and validation tools MUST support SHA-256 and SHA-512 and SHOULD enable SHA-512 by default. bag-info.txt is optional human-use metadata; arbitrary tag files are permitted, but the RFC does not define gallery CSV field semantics. Filesystems/utilities can normalize names differently; normalization-aware comparison is recommended. The RFC addresses corruption, not active attacks.
sources.applicability: Supports inspectable directory packaging and per-deposit integrity checks on ordinary filesystems. The standard does not model corrected asset succession or determine the registrar's intended content set.

sources.title: Oxford Common File Layout Specification
sources.released_version_or_commit: OCFL v1.1 specification family; release tag 1.1.1, commit c3f88b3, shown as Latest at inspection; earlier 1.1.0 remains separately published.
sources.access_utc: UNKNOWN exact request timestamp; independent reviser access occurred within the bounded window in independent_review_access.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official 1.1 specification and inspected object version directories, content and inventory rules, current/root state, digest sidecars, optional version inventories and logs. Read only; no OCFL validator or implementation was run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: OCFL inventories track current state and version history. The object ID remains stable and version directories are continuous; existing versions are expected immutable. Every file in a version content directory must be referenced in that version's inventory. The root inventory MUST exist; version-directory inventories SHOULD be included. Every inventory file that exists MUST have a digest sidecar. The format does not define the gallery's curatorial-completeness rule.
sources.applicability: A transparent filesystem-native object history suitable where successive states and reconstructable versions justify the inventory and validator discipline; a whole-object copy recommendation is local operational guidance.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue records ambiguity over which inventory a content-directory manifest rule refers to. The released rule is sourced to the official change log (S04), not inferred from the issue alone.

sources.title: OCFL specification change log and release history
sources.released_version_or_commit: OCFL 1.1 tag / commit 4b05472; OCFL 1.1.1 tag / commit c3f88b3. The 1.1.1 tag page displayed the Latest badge at inspection.
locator: Clarify manifest requirements in historic inventories
sources.access_utc: UNKNOWN exact request timestamp; independent reviser access occurred within the bounded window in independent_review_access.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official change log and separate release-tag pages; checked the historic-inventory entry and tag/commit identities. A direct open of the generic releases index returned an internal error, so release identity was confirmed from the individual 1.1 and 1.1.1 tag pages instead. No source code was run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The v1.1.0 change-log entry for #538 says each historical inventory manifest must reference every file in that version directory. The separate v1.1 §3.7 wording makes root inventory MUST and version-directory inventory SHOULD; §3.6 requires a sidecar for every inventory file that exists. v1.1.1 is a later clarification release, not evidence that the v1.1.0 fix was a data-loss repair.
sources.applicability: Establishes released specification history and exact version tags, not third-party validator behavior or an observed gallery recovery incident.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata v3.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: PREMIS v3.0; Library of Congress identifies full data dictionary updated November 2015.
locator: event date, outcome and Object/Agent relations
sources.access_utc: UNKNOWN exact request timestamp; independent reviser access occurred within the bounded window in independent_review_access.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official Library of Congress PDF and inspected fixity and Event/outcome passages. Read only; no PREMIS serialization or validator was run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: PREMIS separates digest algorithm/value from the fixity-check Event and its outcome/date. Event identifiers, type and datetime are mandatory in the data model. Some backup-copy actions may be recorded in system logs rather than as PREMIS events.
sources.applicability: Supports a readable PREMIS-inspired copy/restore event log, not a claim of formal PREMIS conformance.

sources.title: git-annex whereis, log and fsck manuals
sources.released_version_or_commit: Online manuals did not identify a reviewed release; version-sensitive current documentation.
sources.access_utc: UNKNOWN exact request timestamp; independent reviser access occurred within the bounded window in independent_review_access.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the three official manual pages and inspected location reporting, history limits and remote-check options. Read only; git-annex was not installed, configured or run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: whereis reports last-received location information and does not contact remotes. fsck --from normally copies remote content for checksum verification; --fast skips checksum calculations and transfer, checking expected presence. The log's history can be absent under documented forget/private settings.
sources.applicability: Higher-capability content-key/location option for a custodian already prepared to operate Git and annex remotes. Location metadata or --fast alone is not live content-integrity proof; not selected for this pilot.

selected_scw_adjudications.disposition: BagIt for the stated small pilot remains a conditional product choice/inference; no relative-cost threshold or many-revision conclusion is established.
BagIt has no native successor-version model; OCFL has version directories, inventories and state. A separate gallery register remains compatible with BagIt.
Retain the historical-inventory clarification; separately state root inventory MUST, per-version inventory SHOULD and sidecar MUST for each inventory present.
MUST support both SHA-256 and SHA-512; SHOULD enable SHA-512 by default. Actual tool behavior is untested.
